summary.one_liner: LSD (LSDeluxe) is a Rust rewrite of GNU ls that adds colors, icons, tree view, and more formatting options.
summary.what_it_does: It lists directory contents as a replacement for the ls command, with colored output and file-type icons drawn from patched Nerd Font glyphs or Unicode emoji. It supports a tree-view mode (--tree) and other formatting options. Behavior can be customized through optional config.yaml, colors.yaml, and icons.yaml files in ~/.config/lsd (or a custom path via --config-file). Icon overrides can be set by file name, file type, or extension. The README is heavily inspired by the colorls project and includes troubleshooting notes for fonts, Windows LS_COLORS, and terminal rendering.
use_cases: replace ls with a colorful directory listing
view directory trees in the terminal
show file icons in a terminal listing
install a modern ls alternative via package manager
notable: Drop-in ls alternative with colors, icons, and tree view
Customizable via YAML config, colors, and icon override files
Packaged for many OSes including Windows, macOS, BSDs, and Linux distros
Follows XDG config directory spec on Unix
caveats: Icons require a patched Nerd Font or similar font installed and configured in the terminal
Some terminals (e.g. Konsole) trim the first character of names, and PuTTY/KiTTY need 1-character-wide icon fonts
Windows color customization relies on the LS_COLORS environment variable
